proposal: A long bench is divided into two equal left and right zones. Fourteen identical wooden knobs are placed across the zones, seven per zone. In the right zone the knobs form a straight row with one central gap interrupting the line exactly at the middle position. All knobs sit upright on the bench surface. The left zone holds its seven knobs in a continuous row with no gaps. The interruption draws the first glance to the middle of the right zone. Total knobs: 14.

Two equally lit rectangular niches side by side receive eight identical clay discs mounted flat on their back walls. The left niche holds three discs in a loose vertical line along its left edge. The right niche holds the remaining five discs: one centered exactly in the middle, with two discs placed immediately above and two immediately below it, spaced at half the distance of the left-niche arrangement to create visual density at that single point. All eight discs are used once. The total is eight.

On a long bench, divide the surface into two equal zones of seven positions each. Place all fourteen identical wooden knobs in a straight row, one per position, using every knob once. In the right zone only, shift the central knob one inch forward from the line to create a clear spatial break. All other knobs remain aligned. The bench itself holds the full row; no additional items are added. The fourteen knobs total fourteen. This layout directs the first glance to the middle of the right zone.

The window is divided into left and right sections of equal illumination. All twelve identical paper arcs are placed within the right section only. They are arranged in four concentric arcs that tighten progressively toward the lower-left target point, with spacing reduced to half at the innermost ring to create visual density. The left section remains empty. This uses every arc once and totals twelve arcs. The first glance is thereby directed to the lower-left target on the right section.

Position a single window divided into two equal left and right sections under identical lighting. Place all twelve identical paper arcs within the right section only, forming a tight radial fan that converges at the lower-left target point. The six arcs nearest the target overlap their inner edges by half their width to create denser visual mass, while the remaining six extend outward with increasing spacing. No arcs enter the left section. This uses every arc once and totals twelve paper arcs.

A rectangular board is divided vertically into two equal left and right regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed as follows: fourteen pegs form a dense grid filling the right region and the upper two-thirds of the left region; the remaining two pegs sit at the top edge of the left region. This leaves an empty vertical channel running down the left region’s center and terminating at the bottom-left corner. The channel creates a clear visual path that draws the first glance directly to that corner. Every peg is used exactly once. Total pegs: 16.

Two equally lit rectangular niches side by side. Place three clay discs in the left niche, spaced evenly along its vertical midline. In the right niche mount the remaining five discs: one at exact center, with two discs above and two below aligned vertically and spaced at equal intervals to converge on the center. All eight identical discs are used once. The converging placement draws the first glance to the right niche center.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. Twelve identical paper fans are mounted flat across both panels, six per panel. On the left panel, five fans form a continuous arc along the outer edges; the sixth fan is omitted from the center, leaving an empty vertical channel that runs straight from the panel bottom to the top-center point. On the right panel, all six fans are placed in a dense repeating pattern with no gaps. The empty channel on the left panel creates the sole visual interruption, directing the first glance to the top center of the left panel. Total fans used: 12.

Divide the long bench into two equal left and right zones. Position seven identical wooden knobs in a straight row across the left zone. In the right zone position the remaining seven knobs in a straight row but leave an open gap exactly at the zone's middle point. The gap interrupts the row and draws the first glance to that central spot. All fourteen knobs are used once and rest directly on the bench surface.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. On the left panel, nine paper fans are mounted with their handles converging at the top-center point, blades overlapping slightly to create a dense radial cluster. The remaining three fans are spaced evenly across the right panel with no focal overlap. All twelve fans are used once. The concentrated arrangement on the left panel draws the initial glance to its top center while the sparse right-panel placement provides balance without competing focal points. Total fans: 12.

A rectangular felt hanging is divided by a vertical center seam into two equal left and right fields. Ten distinct cards are affixed to the hanging, one in each position, with no overlaps or spares. On the left field, eight cards form a tight cluster whose densest point is the upper-right corner of that field, serving as the target; the remaining two cards occupy the lower-left and lower-right corners of the right field. The cluster draws the first glance to the specified target through proximity and density. Total cards: 10.

Two equally lit rectangular niches side by side receive the eight identical clay discs. Place four discs in the left niche in a loose horizontal row along the back wall. In the right niche, mount the remaining four discs vertically on the back wall so their centers align on a single vertical axis at the niche midpoint, spaced 5 cm apart and centered 10 cm from top and bottom edges. The vertical alignment concentrates visual weight at the right niche center. Total discs: 8.

Divide the felt hanging vertically into equal left and right fields. Position the upper-right target at the top-right corner of the left field. Arrange all ten cards on the hanging by clustering five cards tightly around the target in the left field, with decreasing density toward the field's center and bottom. Place the remaining five cards spaced evenly across the right field. This uses every card once. The total is ten cards.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. On the left panel, nine paper fans are mounted with their handles converging so the fan heads form a tight cluster exactly at the top-center point. The remaining three fans are spaced evenly across the right panel. All twelve fans are identical, used once, and oriented to face forward. The concentrated grouping on the left panel draws the first glance to its top center while the sparser right panel provides balance. Total elements: 12 fans.

Divide the long bench into two equal left and right zones. Position all 14 identical wooden knobs in a single row spanning both zones, with seven knobs per zone. In the left zone, space the knobs evenly at 20 cm intervals. In the right zone, space the outer knobs at 20 cm but reduce spacing to 8 cm intervals approaching the exact center, creating a visual convergence at the middle of the right zone. The total number of knobs is 14. This arrangement uses every knob once and places each supplied element in its designated position along the bench.

Mount twelve identical paper arcs inside a single window divided into two equal vertical sections of identical lighting. Position eleven arcs in the left section to form continuous concentric curves flowing rightward. In the right section, place the twelfth arc alone in the lower-left quadrant but with a 2 cm gap interrupting its curve at the exact target point. All arcs are used once. The gap creates the sole visual break, directing first glance to the lower-left target on the right section. Total: 12 arcs.

A rectangular felt hanging is divided by a vertical center line into two equal left and right fields. Ten distinct cards are placed once each: the target card occupies the upper-right corner of the left field; three additional cards are positioned immediately adjacent to it (one directly above, one to its left, one diagonally lower-left) to create a tight cluster; the remaining six cards are distributed singly across the right field at even intervals. The left-field cluster draws the first glance to the designated upper-right target. Total cards used: 10.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. On the left panel, six paper fans are arranged in a tight radial cluster whose handles converge at the top-center point; the remaining six fans occupy the right panel in a loose horizontal row along its lower edge. All twelve fans are identical and used once. The dense convergence on the left panel creates a focal zone at its top center, directing the first glance precisely there before the eye drifts rightward. Total fans: 12.

Divide the board vertically into equal left and right regions. Position all sixteen identical pegs exclusively within the left region, arranged in four rows of four that progressively tighten toward the bottom-left corner so the densest cluster sits precisely at that corner. This uses every peg once. The two regions remain empty on the right and sparsely occupied on the upper left. Total pegs: 16.

Two equal window sections side by side. Place eight arcs in the left section forming four parallel vertical curves spaced evenly. In the right section place the remaining four arcs: three stacked vertically on the right edge and one isolated arc positioned at the lower-left target, creating a clear break in alignment and spacing from the others. All arcs oriented identically as 90-degree segments. Total arcs: 12.

Two equally lit rectangular niches receive all eight identical clay discs. Position four discs in the left niche as a uniform 2x2 grid filling the space. In the right niche mount the remaining four discs at the corners only, leaving a clear vertical channel of empty space through the center. This interruption directs the first glance straight to the center of the right niche. Every disc is used once. Total: 8.

A rectangular board is divided by a central vertical line into two equal left and right regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed as follows: seven pegs form a horizontal row across the top of the left region; seven pegs form a matching row across the top of the right region; one peg is placed at the bottom-left corner of the left region; one peg is placed at the bottom-right corner of the right region. A clear vertical gap one peg-width wide runs down the center of the left region from the top row to the single bottom peg, interrupting the otherwise regular spacing. All sixteen pegs are used. The interruption gap directs the first glance straight to the bottom corner of the left region. Total pegs: 16.

A long bench is divided into two equal left and right zones. Fourteen identical wooden knobs are placed across both zones, seven per zone. In the right zone the knobs form a straight row with regular spacing except for one open gap centered at the middle, creating an interruption that draws the first glance there. The left zone holds its seven knobs in unbroken regular spacing. All fourteen knobs are used once. The bench supports the entire arrangement. Total: 14 knobs.

A rectangular board is divided vertically into two equal left and right regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed on the board such that their spacing decreases steadily toward the bottom-left corner of the left region, forming converging rows that tighten at that single point. The right region receives the remaining pegs in wider, uniform spacing. All sixteen pegs are used exactly once. The total is sixteen pegs.

The felt hanging is divided vertically into two equal rectangular fields. Position the left field as the primary area and the right field as secondary. Place one card at the upper-right corner of the left field to mark the target. Arrange the remaining nine cards in two diagonal lines that run across both fields but terminate abruptly with a clear gap directly at the target card, creating an open band interruption. All ten cards are used once. The felt serves as the uniform background substrate. Total elements: 10 cards plus 1 hanging.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. Twelve identical paper fans are mounted across both: seven on the left panel and five on the right. On the left panel, six fans form a radial arc around the top-center point with their handles pointing outward; the seventh fan is placed exactly at that top-center point, its open blades creating a clear radial gap that interrupts the surrounding arc. The five fans on the right panel are arranged in a continuous vertical row with no gaps. All twelve fans are used once. The interruption at the left panel's top center draws the first glance there.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. The left panel receives seven paper fans: six form a dense radial burst from its top-center point outward, leaving an empty vertical channel exactly at that top-center spot. The right panel receives the remaining five fans in a uniform grid filling its entire surface. All twelve fans are identical, fully deployed, and mounted flat. The empty channel on the left panel interrupts the surrounding fan pattern, directing the first glance to the top center of the left panel. Total fans used: 12.

On a long bench divide the surface into two equal left and right zones. Position all fourteen identical wooden knobs in a single straight row, seven per zone, spaced at identical intervals. At the exact middle of the right zone insert one extra gap equal to two normal intervals, breaking the otherwise uniform sequence while using every knob once. This single break draws the first glance directly to that central right-zone position. Total: 14 knobs.

A rectangular board is divided by a vertical midline into two equal square regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed as follows: fourteen pegs form a uniform grid filling the right region completely. In the left region, thirteen pegs form a matching grid, while the fourteenth peg is omitted from the bottom-left corner, creating a clear gap that interrupts the grid pattern. The empty space draws the first glance directly to that bottom corner. All sixteen pegs are used once. Total: 16.

On the long bench divide the surface into two equal zones side by side. Position seven identical wooden knobs in the left zone in a straight row parallel to the bench edge. In the right zone arrange the remaining seven knobs into a tight radial fan whose apex sits exactly at the middle of that zone; the outer knobs of the fan touch the zone boundaries while the central knob marks the apex. Every knob is used once. The radial placement concentrates the first glance at the middle of the right zone. Total knobs: 14.

Two equally lit rectangular niches side by side receive eight identical clay discs mounted flat on their back walls. Place three discs in the left niche, spaced evenly in a horizontal row at mid-height. In the right niche, mount the remaining five discs in a tight vertical cluster centered exactly at the niche midpoint, with each disc edge touching the next to form a compact mass 20 cm wide. All discs sit at identical height and depth. The denser grouping in the right niche draws the first glance to its center. Total discs: 8.

Two equally lit rectangular niches receive the eight identical clay discs. Place three discs in the left niche, spaced evenly along the back wall. In the right niche, position the remaining five discs: four form a broken ring around the exact center, leaving an open radial gap from the niche's front edge straight to the center; the fifth disc sits at the center. This gap interrupts the surrounding arrangement and directs the first glance inward. Total discs: 8.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. Twelve identical paper fans are placed as follows: six on the left panel and six on the right panel. On the left panel, four fans lie horizontally along the bottom edge and two fans lie vertically along the outer side edge, leaving an unobstructed vertical channel from bottom center upward to the top center. On the right panel, all six fans are clustered along the bottom edge. The fans are secured flat to the panels with their handles aligned to the edges. This arrangement uses every fan once and totals twelve fans.

Place all twelve identical paper arcs within the right section of the window. Cluster eight arcs tightly together at the lower-left target point of that section to form a dense focal mass. Position the remaining four arcs singly at the upper-right, upper-left, lower-right, and center of the same section, each spaced at least one arc-length away from the cluster and from one another. The left section remains empty. Every arc is used once. Total: twelve.

Two identical rectangular panels stand side by side. Twelve identical paper fans are arranged across both: nine on the left panel clustered with blades overlapping and tips converging tightly at the top-center point to create visual density; the remaining three on the right panel spaced evenly apart. All fans are oriented with handles pointing outward. The left-panel cluster occupies the upper third, drawing the eye immediately to its densest point. Total elements: 12 fans + 2 panels = 14.

A rectangular board is divided by a vertical midline into two equal regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed as follows: fourteen pegs form two parallel horizontal rows of seven across the upper half of the right region; the remaining two pegs sit at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners of the left region, leaving an empty vertical corridor from the top edge straight down to the lower-left corner. This corridor creates a clear visual interruption that funnels the first glance along its length to the target corner. Total pegs used: 16.

Place all twelve identical paper arcs inside the single window's right section only. Cluster them densely together at the lower-left target so the arcs overlap and pack tightly in that spot while the remaining space in the right section stays clear. Leave the left section empty of arcs. The two sections remain equally lit. Every arc is used exactly once. Total: 12 arcs.

A rectangular felt hanging is divided vertically into two equal fields. Ten distinct cards are placed once each: nine form a regular diagonal grid across both fields, while the tenth card creates an open band that interrupts the grid precisely at the upper-right corner of the left field, which is the designated target. The remaining cards occupy the other positions to complete the grid without repetition. This uses all ten cards and both fields. Total cards: 10.

Divide the felt hanging vertically into equal left and right fields. Arrange nine cards in continuous diagonal rows across both fields. Position the tenth card to break the row at the upper-right corner of the left field, creating an open gap. All ten cards are used once. The felt hanging forms the base. Total elements: 11.

The window is divided into two equally lit left and right sections. Eleven identical paper arcs form continuous diagonal lines across the right section, converging toward but stopping short of its lower-left corner to create a single open band. The twelfth arc is placed alone in the left section's upper area. This positions the open band exactly at the lower-left target on the right section. All twelve arcs are used once. Total: 12.

Two equally lit rectangular niches receive all eight identical clay discs. Left niche holds three discs in a tight triangular cluster at its upper left. Right niche holds the remaining five: one centered exactly at its middle, with two discs above-left and two below-right leaving an unobstructed vertical channel 15 cm wide straight to the center disc. Every disc is used once. The channel interrupts the surrounding placement, directing first glance to the right niche center. Total discs: 8.

Position a single vertical window divided into two equal side-by-side sections, both lit identically. Place all twelve identical paper arcs within the window. In the left section, form a continuous radial fan of six arcs converging toward the shared center line. In the right section, repeat the same fan with the remaining six arcs but leave a clear gap interrupting the lowest arc at the lower-left quadrant of that section; this gap is the target. The interruption breaks the otherwise regular curve, directing first glance precisely there. Total arcs used: twelve.

Divide the board into two equal left and right rectangular regions. Position all sixteen identical pegs on the board such that twelve form converging diagonal rows leading into the bottom-left corner of the left region while the remaining four occupy the right region in a sparse grid. The left-region pegs are spaced progressively closer together as they approach the target corner. Every peg is used exactly once. Total: 16.

Two identical rectangular niches sit side by side at eye level, both evenly lit from above. The left niche receives four clay discs fixed at its four corners. The right niche receives the remaining four clay discs: three placed at the top-left, top-right, and bottom-left corners, leaving the exact center empty. This creates an unobstructed vertical channel from the niche's top edge straight to the vacant center. All eight discs are used once. The clear central channel in the right niche interrupts the surrounding pattern and draws the first glance directly to that center point. Total discs: 8.

A rectangular felt hanging 60 cm wide by 40 cm high is divided by a central vertical seam into two equal 30 cm fields. Ten distinct cards are placed on the hanging, one in each assigned position: four cards clustered tightly around the upper-right target point in the left field (two above, two below the exact center of that quadrant), three cards spaced evenly along the left field's lower half, and three cards distributed across the right field. The denser grouping of cards creates visual concentration that directs the first glance to the upper-right target. Total elements: 1 hanging + 10 cards = 11.

A long bench is divided into two equal left and right zones. Seven wooden knobs are spaced evenly across the left zone. In the right zone the seven remaining knobs are arranged so that spacing narrows progressively toward the exact center knob, creating a visual concentration of density at that single point. All fourteen knobs are used once. The tighter grouping draws the first glance directly to the middle of the right zone. Total: 14 knobs.

A rectangular board is divided by a vertical midline into equal left and right regions. Sixteen identical pegs are placed only in the left region, arranged in four converging rows that narrow toward its bottom-left corner. The top row holds two pegs near the midline; each lower row adds pegs while shifting them progressively leftward and downward, with the bottom row containing six pegs clustered tightly at the target corner. The right region remains empty. All sixteen pegs are used exactly once. This density gradient draws the first glance directly to the bottom corner of the left region. Total pegs: 16.

A rectangular felt hanging is divided by a vertical center seam into two equal square fields. Nine cards form continuous diagonal rows across both fields. The tenth card is placed alone in the upper-right corner of the left field, separated by a 15 cm open band from the nearest card in its row. This isolates the target position. All ten cards are used once. The felt hanging forms the full background. Total: 10 cards.
